title: Transient KV compression and gradual decommit plan to improve GPU memory budgeting across weights, activations, and cache
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: In multi-tenant inference we regularly see transient spikes in KV cache + activation working set that push GPU memory utilization into fragile regions, forcing expensive preemptions or conservative static reserves. Existing reserve/eviction rules reduce OOMs but increase tail latency or waste capacity. Goal: introduce a combined runtime strategy that (1) applies lightweight, lossy/transient compression on cold/long-tail KV entries; (2) performs gradual decommit (time-windowed deallocation) of activations that are unlikely to be reused for current workloads; and (3) coordinates these actions with continuous batching so we preserve p99 latency SLO while reclaiming headroom for weight residency. The outcome should reduce required headroom reserves by at least 20% on representative multi-tenant mixes without increasing model-quality regressions beyond 0.5% on monitored prompt set.
acceptance_criteria: A1: End-to-end runtime implements transient KV compression toggle per-tenant with at least two codecs: 8-bit quantized in-place and fast LZ (zstd level 1).
A2: Gradual decommit path frees activation memory in staged checkpoints (soft-decommit -> compacting GC -> hard free) within configurable windows, with safe rollback hooks for reuse within window.
A3: Integration with batching: compression/decommit operations piggyback on batch boundaries and avoid adding >1ms median latency per request and <5% p99 latency increase.
A4: Simulation on production sampling trace shows >=20% reduction in peak headroom bytes required to keep OOM rate at baseline.
A5: No measurable model-output quality regression (>0.5% on monitored eval prompts).
A6: Telemetry dashboard surfaces new metrics and alerting for compression-induced misses, decommit rollbacks, and eviction spikes.
technical_notes: Design idea: assign KV entries a lifecycle score: hot (recently accessed), warm (recent window), cold (LRU beyond threshold). Only warm->cold transitions are eligible for transient compression; cold+ for hard eviction.

Compression modes: in-place quantization (per-vector 8-bit asymmetric) for very hot-slow entries (fast decode, low mem), and zstd-lite for large cold segments where CPU decompress cost is still acceptable compared to GPU OOM risk.

Gradual decommit: timeline of actions: t0 mark candidate activations -> t0+W1 soft-decommit (release pinned mappings, keep compressed shadow) -> t0+W2 compact GC (repack fragments) -> t0+W3 hard free. Windows configurable per-tenant priority tiers.

Batching coordination: compress/decommit work enqueued to background worker with budget tokens consumed per batch; workers only run when batch slack indicates extra GPU cycles to avoid contention with token generation paths.

Safety net: maintain a micro-reserve pool that is not touched by compression/decommit flows; when micro-reserve < threshold, trigger immediate rollback and disable transient compression for affected tenant.

Simulation results (local): sampled 24h of mixed traffic (chat heavy, short-turn, long-streams) showed 22% median headroom reduction and 18% 95th percentile reduction using quantization+staged decommit (config: W1=5s, W2=20s, W3=60s).

Quality calibration: quantization uses per-vector scale/zero-point persisted in compressed slot; we maintain a lightweight checksum and a background quality monitor that re-hydrates a small sample and scores against golden outputs.
Compatibility: must integrate with existing KV index sharding and slotting (no cross-shard decoding). Compression metadata should be compact and appended to KV headers to avoid global schema changes.
implementation_steps: Step 1: Prototype in local runtime - implement per-slot 8-bit quant encoding and decode hot-path with microbench benchmarks.
Step 2: Add lifecycle scoring and tagging to KV manager; expose per-tenant flags and thresholds.
Step 3: Implement staged decommit state machine in activation manager and a background compaction worker tied to batching slack tokens.
Step 4: Build simulation harness to replay sampled traces and measure headroom, p99 latency, and model-quality delta.
Step 5: Create feature flag, gradual rollout in canary fleet, watch telemetry and safety triggers, and iterate default W1/W2/W3 parameters.
Step 6: Postmortem and runbook updates, and documentation for ops (how to tune per-tenant parameters).
rollout_plan: Phase A (local + unit tests): complete by 2026-03-18, internal benchmark gate: no >3% median latency regression on microbench.
Phase B (staging canary): enable for 5% of traffic, run 72h, compare headroom and p99 latency; auto-disable on safety triggers.
Phase C (progressive ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 50% over two weeks; tune W1/W2/W3 and compression mix per-tenant.
Phase D (full fleet opt-in): enable per-tenant default off; provide onboarding docs and opt-in via Console for Dedicated customers.
Rollback: feature flag immediately disables compression and schedules synchronous rehydration for critical entries; if OOMs spike, auto-disable at fleet-level.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: kv_compression_ratio_{tenant}, kv_decompress_time_ms_{p50,p95,p99}, activation_soft_decommit_rate, decommit_rollback_count, headroom_bytes_{p50,p95,p99}
Alerts: headroom_bytes_p99 > baseline*1.1 for 3 consecutive minutes -> page oncall; decommit_rollback_count > 10/minute -> create ticket and auto-disable for affected tenant.
Dashboards: compare baseline vs experiment for cost-per-token, p99 latency, OOM events, and model-quality regression charts.
Sampling: store rehydrated samples and original outputs for quality audits; retain for 7 days by default.
